# Voice report C — reading order #50–#74 (Jahee … Ungjin Commandery)

Notes on anchors: where a paragraph carries image `at` fragments, the rewrite keeps those exact phrases (listed as **anchors kept**). Where a fix needs a new `at`, it says so.

### Jahee (#50)
- **b0** — names: 3 (Yushin, Bupmin, Kim Seonpum) + office "junior Pajinchan". Why it glazes: rank title strung after a name, first line of the entry.
  - Before: "Yushin posts Bupmin as junior Pajinchan under Kim Seonpum — a countryside season with a tide book instead of a yard. The quay does not care that he is a prince…"
  - After (EN): "Yushin sends Bupmin to the coast to work under Kim Seonpum. It is a season with a tide book instead of a training yard. The quay does not care that he is a prince. It cares whether the sums close."
  - After (KO): "유신은 법민을 바닷가로 보내 김선품 밑에서 일하게 한다. 연무장 대신 조수 장부를 붙든 한 철이다. 항구는 그가 왕자든 말든 상관없다. 셈이 맞는지만 따진다."
- **b1** — names: 4 (Jahee, 자희, Jayi, Seonpum). Why it glazes: hangul gloss in the English, and the "later called Jayi" reveal is told again in b8.
  - Before: "Her name is Jahee — 자희. The court will later call her Queen Jayi. Tonight she is the daughter who keeps Seonpum’s inkstones…"
  - After (EN): "Her name is Jahee. Tonight she is the daughter who keeps Seonpum’s inkstones, and she has already decided his arithmetic is sloppy."
  - After (KO): "그녀의 이름은 자희다. 오늘 밤 그녀는 선품의 벼루를 지키는 딸이고, 그의 셈이 헐겁다고 이미 결론을 내렸다."
- **b10** — names: 5 (Sunduk, Jinduk, Bupmin, Hwarang, Surabol). Why it glazes: two reigns and a city stacked into one opening clause.
  - Before: "Through the remaining years of Queen Sunduk — and into Jinduk’s quieter crown — Bupmin rides with the Hwarang. He does not become the best gyuku player in Surabol…"
  - After (EN): "Two queens come and go. Bupmin rides with the Hwarang through both. He never becomes the best gyuku player in Surabol. He becomes the one who remembers why the game was invented. When “a king for all” finally fits a grown mouth, the words already have dust on them."
  - After (KO): "여왕 둘이 오고 간다. 법민은 그 내내 화랑과 함께 말을 달린다. 서라벌 최고의 격구 선수는 끝내 못 된다. 대신 그 놀이가 왜 생겼는지 기억하는 사람이 된다. ‘모두의 왕’이라는 말이 마침내 다 큰 입에 맞을 무렵, 그 말엔 이미 먼지가 앉아 있다."

### Hyukgose (#51)
- **b1** — names: 8 (Najeong, Yangsan, Alpyung, Sobuldori, Jibekho, Gurema, Jita, Hojin). Why it glazes: six-chief roll call in a parenthesis; four of them never speak. It also hands over the egg before the scene in b4–b11 earns it. **Anchors kept:** "the horse knelt and cried", "The shell opened on a boy".
  - Before: "At Najeong well in Yangsan the horse knelt and cried; the six chiefs — Alpyung, Sobuldori, Jibekho, Gurema, Jita, Hojin — dug where it stood and lifted a great egg…"
  - After (EN): "At a well in the hills, the horse knelt and cried. Six chiefs dug where it stood. They lifted out a great egg. The shell opened on a boy who already looked like a king. He learns fast. The chiefs say the land has been waiting."
  - After (KO): "산골 우물가에서 말이 무릎을 꿇고 울었다. 여섯 촌장이 그 자리를 팠다. 큰 알 하나가 나왔다. 껍질이 갈라지자, 벌써 임금 얼굴을 한 사내아이가 있었다. 배우는 게 빠르다. 촌장들은 이 땅이 그를 기다려 왔다고 한다."
- **b20** — names: 6 (Lee, Jung, Choi, Son, Bae, Seol). Why it glazes: a surname list read like a textbook caption. **Anchor kept (KO):** "여섯 가문이 정치를 쥔다".
  - Before: "The six clans of Lee, Jung, Choi, Son, Bae, Seol dominate politics."
  - After (EN): "Six families end up running everything. In every new country, six families always do."
  - After (KO): "여섯 가문이 정치를 쥔다. 새 나라는 어디든, 결국 여섯 가문이 쥔다."

### Talhae (#52)
- **b0** — names: 3 (Hyukgosé, Ajinpo) + reign count. Why it glazes: opens on a regnal year instead of the chest. **Anchor kept:** "a chest comes in on the tide at".
  - Before: "In the thirty-ninth year of Hyukgosé, a chest comes in on the tide at Ajinpo with a magpie flying over it, crying."
  - After (EN): "Late in the first king’s reign, a chest comes in on the tide at a fishing beach. A magpie flies over it, crying."
  - After (KO): "첫 임금의 치세도 저물 무렵, 밀물을 타고 궤짝 하나가 갯마을 바닷가로 들어온다. 그 위로 까치 한 마리가 울며 난다."

### Exile (#54)
- **b4** — names: 6 (Daeya, Gyebek, Hundred-Victories, Silla, Gomanaru, Gomanari, Samhan). 136 words. Why it glazes: the signature charge is buried under backstory, a ferry name and a garrison clause. **Anchors kept (all nine stills):** "goes looking for the general", "He leaves the line to other men", "the fastest thing on four legs in Samhan", "rides him flat along the neck like a thrown knife", "starts to turn his horse", "does not finish turning", "One cut on the pass.", "a speck on the far ridge", "nobody left to tell it what to do".
  - Before: "They have watched him work. In the border years after Daeya, Gyebek earned the name Hundred-Victories mostly one way, and the Silla garrison towns learned to dread it. He leaves the line to other men…"
  - After (EN): "They have watched him work. On the border, Gyebek earned his nickname mostly one way. He leaves the line to other men and goes looking for the general. His black horse, Gomanari, is the fastest thing on four legs in Samhan. Gyebek rides him flat along the neck like a thrown knife, the blade reversed along his forearm. The general sees a black shape where the field was empty. He starts to turn his horse, and does not finish turning. One cut on the pass. By the time the escort draws, the black horse is a speck on the far ridge. An army stands in a field with nobody left to tell it what to do."
  - After (KO): "그들은 그가 일하는 걸 본 적이 있다. 국경에서 계백이 그 별명을 얻은 방식은 대개 하나였다. 진은 남들에게 맡기고, 그는 장수를 찾아간다. 검은 말 고마나리는 삼한에서 네 발 달린 것 중 가장 빠르다. 계백은 던진 칼처럼 그 목에 납작 엎드려 달린다. 칼날은 거꾸로 쥐어 팔뚝을 따라 눕혔다. 장수는 비어 있던 들판에 검은 것이 나타난 걸 본다. 말머리를 돌리기 시작하고, 끝내 다 돌리지 못한다. 스치며 한 번 벤다. 호위들이 칼을 뽑을 즈음 검은 말은 먼 능선 위의 점이다. 한 군대가, 무엇을 하라고 말해 줄 사람 하나 없이 들판에 서 있다."
- **b48** — names: 2 (Chunbok, Baekje) + "eleven years later". Why it glazes: repeats b39’s "cannot countermand", and the numbered flash-forward contradicts *Coup*, where Chunbok says "Baekje will fall on its own" the same year.
  - Before: "The king is still in mourning and cannot countermand what the clans wrote with his borrowed seal — and eleven years later it will be Chunbok, of all men, who tells a different king that Baekje falls on its own."
  - After (EN): "Remember the young Satek who just called it His Majesty’s will. He will say worse things in His Majesty’s name, later, to a much bigger king."
  - After (KO): "방금 ‘전하의 뜻’이라 말한 사택 집안 젊은이를 기억해 두라. 그는 나중에, 훨씬 큰 임금 앞에서, 전하의 이름으로 더한 말을 한다."

### Three Princes (#57)
- **b2** — names: 5 (Great Lady, Yang, Go, Bu, Samseonghyeol). Why it glazes: ends on a place-name gloss after a dash. **Anchor kept:** "three divine princes named".
  - Before: "Long after the Great Lady’s stone sons, three divine princes named Yang, Go, and Bu arise from the well — Samseonghyeol."
  - After (EN): "Long after the Great Lady’s stone sons, three divine princes named Yang, Go and Bu climb out of a hole in the ground."
  - After (KO): "할망의 돌 아들들이 생기고 한참 뒤, 양·고·부라는 세 신인이 땅속 구멍에서 기어 나온다."
- **b11** — names: 2 (Tamla, Baekje). Why it glazes: a treaty summary in a fairy tale.
  - Before: "Since then, Tamla has been an ally of Baekje, sending tribute and troops when needed."
  - After (EN): "Ever since, the island has sent Baekje oranges and, when asked, men."
  - After (KO): "그 뒤로 섬은 백제에 귤을 보내고, 부르면 사람도 보낸다."

### Kangrim (#60)
- **b2** — names: 3 (Kimchi, Kangrim, King Yumla). Why it glazes: a whole myth crammed into fragments ("three beads in the ash, swallowed"), so the reader can’t tell who swallowed what. **Anchors kept:** "Three flowers on the water", "King Yumla".
  - Before: "A magistrate named Kimchi had a murder the living law could not try. Three brothers, killed for the silk on their backs and sunk in a pond. Three flowers on the water, three beads in the ash, swallowed…"
  - After (EN): "A magistrate named Kimchi had a murder he could not try. Three brothers were killed for their silk and sunk in a pond. They came back as three flowers on the water. Burned, they became three beads. A woman swallowed them and bore three sons. The sons came home from the exams and died in one bow. Their mother would not stop writing petitions. So Kimchi sent his strongest man, Kangrim, to bring King Yumla up and close the case."
  - After (KO): "김치 원님에게는 산 자의 법으로 못 닫는 살인이 있었다. 형제 셋이 비단 때문에 죽어 연못에 가라앉았다. 셋은 물 위의 꽃 셋으로 돌아왔다. 태우니 구슬 셋이 되었다. 한 여인이 그걸 삼키고 아들 셋을 낳았다. 아들들은 과거 보고 돌아와 절하다 한꺼번에 죽었다. 어미는 소지를 멈추지 않았다. 그래서 원님은 제일 센 사내 강림을 보내, 염라대왕을 끌어올려 사건을 닫게 했다."
  - (Fix the capital T in "Three flowers" mid-sentence by changing the `kr-ink-three-flowers` anchor to "three flowers on the water".)
- **b5** — names: 4 (Kangrim, Haewonmek, King Yumla, gate-god/kitchen-god). Why it glazes: a 20-word appositive on Haewonmek’s job history. **Anchors kept:** "he shut his eyes and jumped", "stood up at the underworld gate", "with court courtesy", "King Yumla".
  - Before: "Kangrim’s wife kept the gate-god and the kitchen-god fed, and they put him on the road. At the last pond he shut his eyes and jumped… Haewonmek, the fetch who had been at it before the island had a second name for the office…"
  - After (EN): "His wife kept the gate-god and the kitchen-god fed, so they put him on the road. At the last pond he shut his eyes and jumped, and stood up at the underworld gate. Someone was already walking that road with a red book. Haewonmek, the oldest fetch there is. Kangrim asked the way. Haewonmek pointed, and kept walking. Kangrim waited, and addressed King Yumla with court courtesy."
  - After (KO): "아내가 문신과 조왕을 잘 먹인 덕에, 신들이 그를 길에 올려 주었다. 마지막 연못에서 그는 눈을 감고 뛰어들었고, 저승문 앞에 서 있었다. 그 길엔 이미 붉은 책을 든 이가 걷고 있었다. 해원맥. 세상에서 제일 오래된 차사다. 강림이 길을 물었다. 해원맥은 손으로 가리키고, 계속 걸었다. 강림은 기다렸다가 염라대왕을 조정의 예로 불렀다."

### Tribute (#61)
- **b1** — names: 3 (Dongseong, Baekje, Muju). Why it glazes: a king’s name and a harbour nobody meets again.
  - Before: "King Dongseong of Baekje takes an army as far as Muju harbour and stops there, and lets word go across the water on its own…"
  - After (EN): "Baekje’s king marches an army to the southern harbour and stops. He lets the news cross the water on its own. It gets there faster than he would have."
  - After (KO): "백제 임금이 군사를 이끌고 남쪽 포구까지 가서 멈춘다. 소문이 제 발로 바다를 건너게 둔다. 소문이 그보다 빨리 닿는다."

### Coup (#62)
- **b17** — names: 2 (Euija, Assembly) + "eight houses". Why it glazes: a 30-word dash clause listing techniques. **Anchor kept:** "of his own sons to the Assembly, firing every single existing member".
  - Before: "Euija names forty-one of his own sons to the Assembly, firing every single existing member. Eight houses spent four generations sharpening techniques against one another — marriages, roads, clerks planted…"
  - After (EN): "Euija names forty-one of his own sons to the Assembly, firing every single existing member. Eight houses spent four generations sharpening tricks on each other. Marriages. Roads. Clerks planted in rival counting-rooms. In one morning the king clears the board. He simply changes the pieces. By noon nobody has an answer."
  - After (KO): "의자는 제 아들 마흔하나를 좌평에 앉히고, 기존 인사를 모조리 내친다. 여덟 가문은 네 대에 걸쳐 서로를 겨눈 수를 갈아 왔다. 혼인. 길. 상대 계산방에 심어 둔 서기. 왕은 하루아침에 판을 쓸어 버린다. 그냥 말을 바꿔 버린 것이다. 정오가 되어도 받아칠 말이 없다."
- **b18** — names: 4 (Ye family, Bear Fortress, Geum, Ye Sikjin). Why it glazes: a river name inside the fortress clause; the plant (the drawer) gets lost at the end.
  - Before: "Forty-one sons need forty-one seats. None of them goes to the Ye family, which has held Bear Fortress on the Geum for four generations and has never once been asked to court…"
  - After (EN): "Forty-one sons need forty-one seats. None goes to the Ye family. They have held Bear Fortress for four generations and never once been asked to court. Ye Sikjin reads the list at home, twice. Then he puts it in a drawer."
  - After (KO): "아들 마흔하나에게는 자리 마흔하나가 필요하다. 예씨 몫은 하나도 없다. 네 대째 웅진성을 지켜 왔건만 조정에 한 번도 불려 간 적 없는 집안이다. 예식진은 집에서 명단을 두 번 읽는다. 그리고 서랍에 넣는다."
- **b19** — names: 3 (Baekje, White River, Yamato). Why it glazes: a colon list of revenue streams.
  - Before: "With the Assembly remade, he redistributes the quiet wealth that actually runs Baekje: coastal warehouses, pilot fees on the White River, the right to stamp a ship’s pass…"
  - After (EN): "Then he hands out the quiet money that really runs Baekje. Harbour warehouses. River pilot fees. The stamp a ship needs before it sails east. The martial law was the noise. The stamps are what change."
  - After (KO): "그다음 그는 백제를 실제로 굴리는 조용한 돈을 다시 나눈다. 바닷가 창고. 강의 도선료. 동쪽으로 떠나는 배에 찍는 도장. 계엄은 소음이었다. 바뀌는 건 도장이다."
- **b25** — names: 2 (Satek Chunbok, Enabling Law) + gloss "(상좌평)" in English. Why it glazes: hangul gloss on the page. **Anchors kept:** "Satek Chunbok is named Premier", "The Enabling Law did not abolish the chair". Change `euija-coup-chunbok-pm` anchor from "is named Premier (상좌평)" to "is named Premier".
  - Before: "Satek Chunbok is named Premier (상좌평). His own clan finds out at the same time as everyone else…"
  - After (EN): "Satek Chunbok is named Premier. His own clan finds out with everyone else. The Enabling Law did not abolish the chair. It only changed who sits in it."
  - After (KO): "사택천복이 상좌평에 오른다. 제 집안도 남들과 같은 때에 안다. 수권법은 자리를 없애지 않았다. 앉는 사람만 바꿨을 뿐이다."

### Descent (#63)
- **b7** — names: 4 (Heungsu, Silla, Euija, Gomamiji). Why it glazes: a dash aside, then the county name read off the paper, then a fragment list. b8 already names Gomamiji.
  - Before: "Among the first to leave the capital — not by boat, by decree — is Heungsu, who had the bad manners to say the purge would finish what Silla could not…"
  - After (EN): "Among the first sent away, by decree this time, is Heungsu. He had the bad manners to say the purge would finish what Silla could not. Euija calls it a temporary posting. The court knows better. The paper names a county far to the south. Packed earth. A magistrate’s hut with a doorpost for a ring."
  - After (KO): "이번엔 배가 아니라 교지로, 맨 먼저 쫓겨난 사람 가운데 흥수가 있다. 이 숙청이 신라도 못 한 일을 마저 해 줄 거라고, 눈치 없이 말한 사람이다. 의자는 잠시 내려보내는 것이라 한다. 조정은 다 안다. 종이에 적힌 곳은 먼 남쪽 고을이다. 다져진 흙. 칼 고리를 걸 문설주가 남은 원님 오두막."

### Sungchung (#66)
- **b0** — names: 4 (Euija, Silla-Tang, Chunchu Army, Sabi) + a parenthetical gloss. Why it glazes: "(known as…)" is a textbook aside. b3 then repeats the same beat ("panic as the Silla/Tang army is approaching"); cut b3.

### Gyebek (#68)
- **b17** — names: 3 (Gomanari, Ungjin, Tang). Why it glazes: 50 words in one breath with two appositives. Keep the ferry: it pays off in *Yellow Mountain* b119. **Anchor kept:** "a black horse at the post".
  - Before: "He comes out of the house before the light is properly up. The yard is swept. Nothing in it belongs to him any more except a black horse at the post, Gomanari, named for the old bear ferry at Ungjin…"
  - After (EN): "He comes out before the light is properly up. The yard is swept. Nothing in it is his any more except a black horse at the post. Gomanari is named for the bear ferry where Gyebek learned to ride. It is the one thing he owns that the Tang cannot sell in a slave market."
  - After (KO): "날이 채 밝기도 전에 그가 집에서 나온다. 마당은 쓸려 있다. 그 안에 이제 그의 것은 말뚝에 매인 검은 말 한 마리뿐이다. 고마나리. 그가 말 타는 법을 배운 곰나루에서 딴 이름이다. 당이 노예 시장에 내다 팔 수 없는, 그가 가진 단 하나다."
- **b22** — names: 4 (Hundred-Victories, Gyebek, Yellow Mountain, Sabi, Geum). Why it glazes: a merchant aside about river carts hangs off the most important march in the book. **Anchor kept:** "his five thousand set out for the".
  - Before: "Hundred-Victories Gyebek and his five thousand set out for the Yellow Mountain — the inland latch on the road to Sabi, a place merchants have grumbled about for years…"
  - After (EN): "Gyebek and his five thousand set out for the Yellow Mountain. It is the last latch on the road to Sabi. Merchants have cursed its summer dust for years."
  - After (KO): "계백과 그의 오천이 황산으로 떠난다. 사비로 가는 길의 마지막 빗장이다. 장사꾼들이 여름 먼지 때문에 몇 해째 욕하던 곳이다."

### Yellow Mountain (#70)
- **b1** — names: 4 (Samhan, Su Dingfang, Western Turks, qaghan). Why it glazes: a foreign title and a people name stacked onto the man’s debut.
  - Before: "Three years before he ever sees Samhan, Su Dingfang wins a war in a blizzard. He is sixty-five, and the qaghan of the Western Turks has camped for the winter on the reasonable assumption…"
  - After (EN): "Three years before he sees Samhan, Su Dingfang wins a war in a blizzard. He is sixty-five. His enemy has camped for the winter, sure that nobody fights in snow two feet deep. Su marches all night and attacks at dawn. He takes the whole camp before anyone in it has found his boots."
  - After (KO): "삼한을 보기 세 해 전, 소정방은 눈보라 속에서 전쟁 하나를 이긴다. 그는 예순다섯이다. 적은 두 자 깊이 눈 속에서 싸울 놈은 없다고 믿고 겨울 진을 쳤다. 소정방은 밤새 행군해 새벽에 들이친다. 진 안의 누구도 신발을 찾기 전에 진영 전체를 손에 넣는다."
- **b5** — names: 6 (Shandong, Deokmul Island, Silla, Bupmin, Tang) + "660". Why it glazes: the entry’s one narration year, a port and an island, plus troop counts, all in one sentence. The scene header already says "Deokmul Island".
  - Before: "In the sixth month of 660 he sails from Shandong with a hundred and thirty thousand men and drops anchor off Deokmul Island. A Silla fleet of a hundred ships comes out to meet him…"
  - After (EN): "That summer he sails east with a hundred and thirty thousand men and anchors off a small island. A hundred Silla ships come out to meet him. At their head is the crown prince, Bupmin. He is thirty-four, and trying not to stare at the size of the Tang flagship."
  - After (KO): "그해 여름, 그는 십삼만 군사를 싣고 동쪽으로 건너와 작은 섬 앞에 닻을 내린다. 신라 배 백 척이 그를 맞으러 나온다. 맨 앞에 태자 법민이 있다. 서른넷이고, 당나라 기함이 얼마나 큰지 빤히 쳐다보지 않으려 애쓰는 중이다."
- **b13** — names: 5 (Muyeol, Geumdol Fortress, Yushin, Kim Yushin, Tanhyeon, Gyebek). Why it glazes: the reader knows him as Chunchu (he speaks as `chunchu` in b14), and Yushin is named twice. Keep Tanhyeon; Heungsu planted it.
  - Before: "King Muyeol comes as far as Geumdol Fortress and no farther: the field belongs to his son and to Yushin. He sends fifty thousand men west under Kim Yushin with a date in their heads…"
  - After (EN): "The king rides as far as a hill fort and no farther. The field belongs to his son and to Yushin. Fifty thousand men march west with a date in their heads. Between them and the date is the pass at Tanhyeon. Beyond the pass is a man called Gyebek."
  - After (KO): "임금은 산성 하나까지만 오고 더는 오지 않는다. 들판은 아들과 유신의 몫이다. 오만 군사가 머릿속에 날짜 하나를 넣고 서쪽으로 간다. 그들과 그 날짜 사이에 탄현 고개가 있다. 고개 너머에는 계백이라는 사내가 있다."
- **b16** — names: 4 (Tang, White River, Gibeolpo, Baekje). Why it glazes: date plus two names for one river mouth. Keep Gibeolpo; Seongchung’s letter planted it.
  - Before: "On the ninth day of the seventh month the Tang fleet comes into the mouth of the White River at Gibeolpo, where the shore is not a shore at all but a mile of grey mud…"
  - After (EN): "On the ninth day, the Tang fleet sails into the river mouth at Gibeolpo. The shore there is a mile of grey mud. Baekje’s soldiers wait on the high ground. They watch the first Tang companies wade in up to the thigh."
  - After (KO): "아흐렛날, 당의 함대가 기벌포 강어귀로 들어온다. 그곳 물가는 십 리에 걸친 잿빛 진흙이다. 백제 군사들은 높은 땅에서 기다린다. 당의 첫 부대가 허벅지까지 빠지며 걸어 들어오는 것을 지켜본다."
- **b39** — names: 7 (Yellow Mountain, Hundred-Victories, Tang, White River, Red Fowl, Hwangsan). Why it glazes: three names for two places, and "ground Hundred-Victories will never see again" spends his death before the battle.
  - Before: "Seventh month heat sits on the Yellow Mountain like a second army. Dust rises white off the three roads. Downstream, past ground Hundred-Victories will never see again, Tang sails already crowd the White River mouth…"
  - After (EN): "Seventh-month heat sits on the Yellow Mountain like a second army. Dust rises white off the three roads. Downstream, Tang sails already crowd the river mouth. They are waiting for the inland door to open. This field is that door."
  - After (KO): "칠월의 더위가 황산 위에 두 번째 군대처럼 앉아 있다. 세 길목에서 먼지가 희게 오른다. 하류에서는 당의 돛이 벌써 강어귀를 메운다. 내륙의 문이 열리기를 기다리는 중이다. 이 들판이 그 문이다."
- **b45** — names: 5 (Silla, Yushin, Heumsun, Pumil, Baekje). Why it glazes: one 40-word sentence plus the archer clause. **Anchor kept:** "Yushin centre, Heumsun left, Pumil right" (this keeps the paragraph at four names).
  - Before: "Silla comes on the first time in three columns — Yushin centre, Heumsun left, Pumil right — down the three roads at once, exactly as the arithmetic says to…"
  - After (EN): "Silla comes on the first time in three columns: Yushin centre, Heumsun left, Pumil right. Down the three roads at once, exactly as the arithmetic says. Uphill. In the heat. Into yellow shields set edge to edge. The archers wait to see which column is thickest, and loose at that one. All three camps throw them back into their own dust."
  - After (KO): "신라는 첫 공격을 세 갈래로 해 온다. 가운데 유신, 왼쪽 흠순, 오른쪽 품일. 산수가 시키는 그대로, 세 길로 한꺼번에. 오르막을. 땡볕에. 가장자리를 맞댄 노란 방패를 향해. 궁수들은 어느 줄이 가장 두꺼운지 보고 나서야 그 줄에 쏜다. 세 진영이 그들을 제 먼지 속으로 도로 밀어낸다."
- **b83** — names: 5 (Sadaham, Mugwan, Hwangsan, Bangul, Gwanchang). Why it glazes: two dead boys from another era, named in passing, right before two new ones.
  - Before: "The yard still tells the first class in two names — Sadaham and Mugwan, who swore and did not outlive the swear. Nobody at Hwangsan says the rhyme aloud…"
  - After (EN): "The hwarang yard still tells its oldest story in two names: two boys who swore, and did not outlive the swear. Nobody here says the rhyme aloud. The field supplies it anyway. Bangul rides first. Gwanchang rides second."
  - After (KO): "화랑 마당은 아직도 제일 오래된 이야기를 두 이름으로 전한다. 맹세하고, 그 맹세보다 오래 살지 못한 두 소년. 여기선 아무도 그 노래를 입에 올리지 않는다. 들판이 알아서 채운다. 반굴이 먼저 나간다. 관창이 다음이다."
- **b118** — names: 3 (Silla, Chungsang, Sangyeong). Why it glazes: two ministers the reader never meets.
  - Before: "The Silla clerks count too. Twenty-odd taken alive, the ministers Chungsang and Sangyeong among them…"
  - After (EN): "The Silla clerks count too. Twenty-odd taken alive, two ministers among them. Nobody writes down how many of the five thousand were left to take."
  - After (KO): "신라의 서기들도 센다. 사로잡은 자 스무남은, 그 가운데 좌평 둘. 오천 가운데 사로잡을 사람이 몇이나 남아 있었는지는 아무도 적지 않는다."
- **b21** (not rewritten; flag only) — this is a shot list ("Yellow lacquer holds the palisade… Blue plume cuts yellow lacquer"), which the style rule bans in narration. It also spends the b56 duel early. It anchors nine stills, so a rewrite needs re-anchoring first.

### Sabi (#71)
- **b5** — names: 5 (Sabi, Silla, Tang, Red Fowl, Kim Munyeong) + date. Why it glazes: date, rank title and a one-scene name before the threat lands. Then change b12 to "The officer’s collar is closed again."
  - Before: "Outside Sabi, on the twelfth day of the seventh month, the Silla army reaches the Tang camp two days after the date it was given. The Red Fowl has the Silla commissary officer, Kim Munyeong…"
  - After (EN): "The Silla army reaches the Tang camp two days late. The Red Fowl has the Silla supply officer dragged to his tent gate. They open his collar for the sword."
  - After (KO): "신라군이 약속보다 이틀 늦게 당의 진영에 닿는다. 주작은 신라의 군량 담당 장교를 군막 문 앞으로 끌어낸다. 칼 받을 목깃을 풀게 한다."
- **b10** — names: 2 (Red Fowl, Dong Baoliang). Why it glazes: a Tang staff officer named for one line.
  - Before: "The Red Fowl’s right-hand general, Dong Baoliang, steps on his commander’s foot."
  - After (EN): "The Red Fowl’s second-in-command steps on his commander’s foot."
  - After (KO): "주작의 부장이 제 장군의 발을 슬쩍 밟는다."
- **b18** — names: 4 (Tae, Yung, Munsa, Tang). Why it glazes: three princes in two sentences, and Munsa’s reasoning is a nested clause.
  - Before: "His second son Tae, left behind in the capital, declares himself king the next morning. Yung’s son Munsa looks at the size of the Tang camp, says that a king who runs leaves behind an uncle who will kill…"
  - After (EN): "Euija’s second son, left behind, crowns himself the next morning. A grandson takes one look at the Tang camp and does the sum. An uncle who stays will kill whoever opens the gate. So the grandson climbs down the wall on a rope with his household. Half the city follows him down it."
  - After (KO): "도성에 남은 의자의 둘째가 이튿날 아침 스스로 왕이 된다. 손자 하나가 당의 진영을 한 번 보고 셈을 한다. 남은 숙부는 성문 연 자를 다 죽일 것이다. 그래서 손자는 식솔을 데리고 밧줄을 타고 성벽을 내려간다. 성의 절반이 그 밧줄을 따라 내려간다."
- **b19** — names: 3 (Yung, Satek Chunbok, Bupmin) + "Great Minister". Why it glazes: titles before both names.
  - Before: "Crown Prince Yung comes out of the gate with the Great Minister Satek Chunbok a careful pace behind him. Bupmin has him knelt in the dirt…"
  - After (EN): "The crown prince comes out of the gate. Chunbok walks a careful pace behind him. Bupmin has the prince knelt in the dirt before his horse, and spits in his face."
  - After (KO): "태자가 성문을 나온다. 천복이 조심스레 한 걸음 뒤에서 따른다. 법민은 태자를 제 말 앞 흙바닥에 꿇리고, 그 얼굴에 침을 뱉는다."
- **b31** — names: 4 (Ye Sikjin, Bear Fortress, Euija, Red Fowl). Why it glazes: b30 dramatizes it and b32 quotes it, so the same event is told three times. Recommend **cutting b31**. If a bridge is needed:
  - Before: "Ye Sikjin, the guardian of Bear Fortress, captures Euija and surrenders to the Red Fowl."
  - After (EN): "By morning the king is on his way to the Red Fowl’s tent."
  - After (KO): "아침이 되자 임금은 주작의 군막으로 끌려가고 있다."
- **b34** — (flag) The Falling Flowers cliff is narrated in b24–b25 and again in b34–b38. Pick one telling.
- **b39** — names: 5 (Muyeol, Euija, Red Fowl, Gumil, Mochuk). Why it glazes: "King Muyeol" when the reader knows Chunchu, plus an accomplice nobody meets. Keep Gumil (*King Pungjang* calls back to him). **Anchor kept:** "finally arrives at the scene. He makes Euija pour".
  - Before: "King Muyeol finally arrives at the scene. He makes Euija pour his wineglass, and the Red Fowl’s beside it, and executes the traitors Gumil and Mochuk."
  - After (EN): "Chunchu finally arrives at the scene. He makes Euija pour his wine, and the Tang general’s beside it. Then he settles an old debt. Gumil, the man who opened his daughter’s gate, is put to death."
  - After (KO): "마침내 춘추가 당도한다. 그는 의자에게 제 잔에, 그리고 그 옆 당 장수의 잔에 술을 따르게 한다. 그리고 묵은 빚을 갚는다. 딸의 성문을 열어 준 검일이 목숨을 잃는다."
- **b48** — names: 3 (Tang, Jeongnim Temple, Baekje) + date + storey count. Why it glazes: date, temple and storey stacked before a quote.
  - Before: "On the fifteenth day of the eighth month the Tang carve their victory into the five-storey stone pagoda at Jeongnim Temple, on the first storey, where anyone walking round it has to read it…"
  - After (EN): "A month later the Tang carve their victory into a stone pagoda. They put it low, where anyone walking round has to read it. It calls the conquest a deliverance. About Baekje’s king it says:"
  - After (KO): "한 달 뒤, 당은 돌탑에 제 승리를 새긴다. 탑을 도는 사람이면 누구든 읽을 수밖에 없는 낮은 자리다. 비문은 정복을 구원이라 부른다. 백제의 임금에 대해서는 이렇게 적는다."
- **b57** — names: 5 (Red Fowl, Euija, Liu Renyuan, Sabi, Silla) + date. Why it glazes: a garrison commander with a near-twin name of *Ungjin*’s Liu Rengui.
  - Before: "On the third day of the ninth month the Red Fowl sails for home with Euija, his sons, and twelve thousand captives, leaving Liu Renyuan with ten thousand men…"
  - After (EN): "A month later the Red Fowl sails home with Euija, his sons and twelve thousand captives. He leaves ten thousand men to hold the city. Beside them sits a Silla army that has stopped smiling."
  - After (KO): "한 달 뒤, 주작은 의자와 그 아들들, 포로 만 이천을 싣고 귀국길에 오른다. 성에는 군사 만 명을 남긴다. 그 곁에는 더는 웃어 주지 않는 신라군이 있다."

### Buyeo Euija† (#72)
- **b0** — names: 4 (Luoyang, Zetian Gate, Euija, Third Emperor). Why it glazes: a city and a gate before the man. The entry `place` is `changan` and b21 says "the Tang capital", so Luoyang also contradicts it. **Anchor kept:** "Euija is brought forth before the Third Emperor".
  - Before: "In Luoyang, before the Zetian Gate, Euija is brought forth before the Third Emperor."
  - After (EN): "In the Tang capital, Euija is brought forth before the Third Emperor."
  - After (KO): "당의 도성에서, 의자가 황제 앞에 끌려 나온다."
- **b1** — names: 1 + office string "Court of State Ceremonial". Why it glazes: an office title in the joke’s setup.
  - Before: "First there is paperwork. A clerk of the Court of State Ceremonial hands the prisoner a confession already written out in a fair hand…"
  - After (EN): "First, paperwork. A palace clerk hands the prisoner a confession, already written out in a fair hand. There is a space at the bottom for his name."
  - After (KO): "먼저 서류다. 궁의 서기가 포로에게 자백서를 건넨다. 단정한 글씨로 이미 다 써 놓았다. 맨 아래에 이름 쓸 자리만 비어 있다."
- **b26** — names: 1 (Third Emperor). Why it glazes: an obituary card in a row of four textbook lines (b25–b29).
  - Before: "Once heralded as a bright and promising young prince, then a successful conqueror, he now meets his final moments in the capital of the enemy, humiliated by the Third Emperor and with no authority."
  - After (EN): "He was the bright prince once. Then the conqueror. Now he is a man in his enemy’s capital with nothing left to command."
  - After (KO): "한때 그는 빛나는 왕자였다. 그다음엔 정복자였다. 이제 그는 적의 도성에서, 부릴 것 하나 남지 않은 사내다."
- **b28** — names: 2 (Kyun Hwon, Baekje) + "240 years". Why it glazes: new name and number, and b38 says it again, better.
  - Before: "He catches a glimpse of Kyun Hwon, who will later revive Baekje in 240 years."
  - After (EN): "Somewhere far down the years, a stranger is already reaching for his banner."
  - After (KO): "아득한 세월 저편에서, 누군가 벌써 그의 깃발에 손을 뻗고 있다."

### Kim Chunchu† (#73)
- **b24** — names: 5 (Muyeol, Taejong, Second Emperor, True Bone, Silla). Why it glazes: posthumous and temple names together read like a register entry.
  - Before: "He is given the posthumous name Muyeol, and the temple name Taejong, the same two characters as the Second Emperor’s. He is the first True Bone king Silla ever crowned…"
  - After (EN): "They give him a name for the dead: Muyeol. His temple name borrows the Second Emperor’s two characters. He was the first True Bone king ever crowned. He will be the last man anyone calls a diplomat."
  - After (KO): "그에게 죽은 자의 이름이 붙는다. 무열. 묘호는 이세 황제의 두 글자를 빌렸다. 진골로서 처음 왕관을 쓴 사람이다. 그리고 누군가 외교관이라 부를 마지막 사람이다."
- **b28** — names: 3 epithets (Eternal General, Righteous and Merciful, Euija). Why it glazes: two sobriquets in a row, and the second one is Euija, so he appears under two names in one paragraph.
  - Before: "He knelt to the Eternal General, who despised him for it. He knelt to an emperor, who liked him for it and kept his son. The Righteous and Merciful said he did not fear a man who kneels…"
  - After (EN): "He knelt to Gesomun, who despised him for it. He knelt to an emperor, who liked him for it and kept his son. Euija said he did not fear a man who kneels. Euija was wrong. It took eighteen years and a cup of wine to show him."
  - After (KO): "그는 연개소문에게 무릎을 꿇었고, 개소문은 그 때문에 그를 경멸했다. 황제에게 무릎을 꿇었고, 황제는 그 때문에 그를 아꼈고, 아들을 붙잡아 두었다. 의자는 무릎 꿇는 사내 따윈 두렵지 않다고 했다. 의자가 틀렸다. 그걸 보여 주는 데 열여덟 해와 술 한 잔이 들었다."
- **b31** — names: 2 (Munmu, Samhan) + "(35)" age tag + "not as X, but as Y". Why it glazes: file-card age in parentheses plus the banned construction.
  - Before: "King Munmu (35) takes the throne and vows to unify Samhan — not as an inheritance of revenge, but as the country a six-year-old once named out loud."
  - After (EN): "Bupmin takes the throne. They will call him Munmu. He vows to finish it, for the country a six-year-old once named out loud."
  - After (KO): "법민이 왕위에 오른다. 사람들은 그를 문무라 부를 것이다. 그는 끝을 보겠다고 맹세한다. 여섯 살짜리가 언젠가 소리 내어 이름 붙였던 그 나라를 위해."
- (flag) b3 "Munhee (55)", b6 "Bupmin (35)", b22 "King Muyeol (58) dies." Parenthetical age tags read as a file card. Fold them into the prose or drop them.

### Ungjin Commandery (#74)
- **b1** — names: 6 (Sabi, Tang, Baekje, Bear Ford, Geum, Ungjin, Euija). Why it glazes: the place gets three names (Bear Ford, the Geum, Ungjin) in one clause.
  - Before: "When Sabi fell the Tang drew five commanderies over Baekje like a net over a pond, and put the largest of them at Bear Ford on the Geum, Ungjin, where Euija had been handed over…"
  - After (EN): "When the capital fell, the Tang threw five commanderies over the country like a net over a pond. The biggest knot sits at Bear Fortress, where Euija was handed over. So far the net catches mostly rebels."
  - After (KO): "도성이 떨어지자 당은 연못에 그물을 덮듯 나라 위에 도독부 다섯을 씌웠다. 가장 큰 매듭은 의자가 넘겨진 웅진성에 있다. 아직까지 그 그물에 걸리는 건 대개 반란군이다."
- **b3** — names: 4 (Tang, Sabi, Chang’an, Liu Rengui). Why it glazes: four facts in one sentence about a new man.
  - Before: "The Tang garrison at Sabi is relieved that spring by a man nobody in Chang’an expected to see in uniform again. Liu Rengui is sixty, was stripped of office the year before for losing a grain fleet in a storm…"
  - After (EN): "That spring a new man takes over the Tang garrison. Nobody in Chang’an expected to see him in uniform again. Liu Rengui is sixty. Last year he lost a grain fleet in a storm and was stripped of office. Now he comes east as a commoner in white, to earn it back. In his baggage: the Tang calendar, and the list of names nobody may write."
  - After (KO): "그해 봄, 새 사람이 당의 주둔군을 맡는다. 장안의 누구도 그가 다시 군복을 입을 줄 몰랐다. 유인궤는 예순이다. 지난해 풍랑에 군량선을 잃고 관직을 빼앗겼다. 이제 백의종군으로 죄를 씻으러 동쪽에 왔다. 짐 속에는 당의 역서와, 아무도 써서는 안 될 이름들의 목록이 들어 있다."
- **b8** — names: 6 (Surabol, Munmu, Gyerim, Gyerim Prefecture, Silla, Kim). Why it glazes: a gloss on Gyerim that retells the *Alji* myth in a subordinate clause.
  - Before: "Before long an edict comes to Surabol naming the new king, Munmu, Grand Commander of the Gyerim Prefecture. Gyerim is the old name of Silla, the wood where the first Kim was found…"
  - After (EN): "Then an edict arrives for the new king. It makes him Grand Commander of the Gyerim Prefecture. Gyerim is his country’s oldest name, the wood where a rooster crowed over a golden box. In the edict it is one province of the empire. And the king is its governor."
  - After (KO): "이윽고 새 임금 앞으로 칙서가 온다. 그를 계림주 대도독으로 삼는다는 내용이다. 계림은 이 나라의 가장 오래된 이름이다. 닭이 금궤 위에서 울던 숲. 칙서 안에서 그곳은 제국의 한 고을이다. 그리고 임금은 그 고을 원이다."
- **b20** (flag only) — "launches the Eighth Invasion of Goguryeo" is an ordinal from a textbook. It anchors `gaozong-huanglong-war`, so a fix needs a new anchor. Suggested: "So the Third Emperor goes to war with Goguryeo: his father’s war, inherited with everything else."

## Five worst paragraphs in this range
1. **Exile b4** — 136 words, six names. The book’s signature charge is buried under backstory (all nine anchors can stay).
2. **Ungjin Commandery b1** — one place under three names (Bear Ford, the Geum, Ungjin) in a single clause, at the top of the entry.
3. **Hyukgose b1** — a six-chief roll call in a parenthesis, and it opens the egg before the scene does.
4. **Yellow Mountain b5** — year, port, island, troop count and crown prince in one sentence.
5. **Sabi b18** — three princes (Tae, Yung, Munsa) and a nested argument in two sentences.

- The six chiefs except Alpyung and Sobuldori: Jibekho, Gurema, Jita, Hojin. Also the place Yangsan.
- The six clan surnames as a list: Lee, Jung, Choi, Son, Bae, Seol.
- Okji, Guchu, Dojo (Yuri’s friends).
- Dongseong and Muju (*Tribute*).
- Dong Baoliang, Kim Munyeong, Tae, Munsa, Mochuk, Liu Renyuan (*Sabi*). Liu Renyuan is easily confused with Liu Rengui.
- Chungsang and Sangyeong; Sadaham and Mugwan as a passing aside (*Yellow Mountain*).
- Shandong, Deokmul Island, Geumdol Fortress, the Western Turks/qaghan, Jeongnim Temple, the Zetian Gate, Luoyang, the Court of State Ceremonial.
- Kyun Hwon in *Buyeo Euija†* b28 (keep him once, in b38).
